prerequisites.title: Paid SurveyMonkey plan
prerequisites.detail: Creating and deploying an OAuth app requires a paid plan, per a third-party connector guide. SurveyMonkey's own docs say anyone with an account can register.

prerequisites.title: Review the terms of use
prerequisites.detail: Apps unrelated to surveys, white-labeling, or exporting data to competitors are not permitted. Competitors cannot open a Developer Account.

steps.title: Register the app in Developer Portal
steps.detail: Sign in to the Developer Portal, choose My Apps then Add a New App, and choose Private or Public type. Use a name that does not include 'SurveyMonkey'.

steps.title: Copy the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Get the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and check it matches what you enter in the app's Settings tab.
steps.done_when: The redirect URL is saved in app Settings.

steps.title: Set scopes
steps.detail: Draft the scope list and mark needed scopes Required, optional, or not required. Users must approve all Required scopes or OAuth fails.
inputs: List of API features you need
steps.done_when: Scopes are saved with Update Scopes.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret, which are on the app's Overview tab.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Deploy the private app
steps.detail: Click Deploy on the app page before the 90-day draft window ends.
steps.done_when: The app is deployed and your team can connect.

steps.title: Prepare the app listing
steps.detail: Draft an honest English listing stating scope requirements, whether users need an account with you, and support contacts.

steps.title: Submit the listing for approval
steps.detail: Use the listings tab in My Apps to submit. If you need the two restricted scopes, contact the SurveyMonkey help center with your use case.

steps.title: Wait for SurveyMonkey approval
steps.detail: No review duration is documented. SurveyMonkey may reject based on criteria not on its checklist.
steps.done_when: The app is approved and published.

traps.title: Public apps published in the App Directory can make
traps.detail: Public apps published in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

traps.title: Rate limits are enforced at 100% only after the
traps.detail: Rate limits are enforced at 100% only after the app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days; up to three violations of up to 150% are permitted in a 30-day window.

traps.title: Draft apps are disabled after 90 days
traps.detail: Deploy before the 90-day draft window ends or the app is disabled.

traps.title: Private apps cannot serve outside customers
traps.detail: All users must be on the same SurveyMonkey team with a paid plan. Draft apps work only for the owner.

traps.title: Terms bar AI training on API data
traps.detail: You may not use the API or its content to create, train, or improve AI or machine learning systems, with a narrow exception for inference-time processing. Check this against your agent design.

traps.title: Reselling API access needs approval
traps.detail: Selling or redistributing API access or content to third parties needs SurveyMonkey's written approval.

traps.title: Users may hit paid-plan walls
traps.detail: Accounts without the plan a scope needs are asked to upgrade. Basic plans see only 25 responses per survey.

traps.title: Callback domain is Composio's
traps.detail: SurveyMonkey docs do not say redirect domains are verified, so use the Composio redirect URI directly.

blockers.symptom: Public app is rejected or not approved
blockers.what_it_means: SurveyMonkey can reject for criteria beyond its published checklist.
blockers.what_to_do: Review the checklist, fix the listing, and resubmit or ask the help center.
blockers.agent_can_help: Audit the listing and app name against the checklist.

blockers.what_it_means: Required scopes must be approved and available to the user, which may need a paid plan.
blockers.what_to_do: Mark non-essential scopes optional and tell users which plan is needed.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review scopes and mark which can be optional.

open_questions: How long does App Directory review take? Ask SurveyMonkey developer support; no duration was found.
Are tokens going to expire? They currently do not but may in future; watch developer announcements.
Do you need a paid plan to register an app? Sources disagree; try registering with a free account.
What exactly do reviewers check beyond the public checklist? Ask SurveyMonkey via the help center.

evidence.answer: Unused API calls do not roll over to the next period.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Keep your Access Credentials secure and confidential, as you are solely responsible for any activities occurring under your Developer Account.
evidence.answer: The developer must keep access credentials secure and confidential and is solely responsible for activity under the Developer Account.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey may also issue credentials for your App.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey may also issue credentials for the developer's app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If SurveyMonkey issues an Access Token for your App, you may only use that Access Token with that specific App, and cannot use that Access Token with any other application.
evidence.answer: An access token issued for an app may only be used with that specific app.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Apps which are not related to facilitating surveys (e.g. you may not use SurveyMonkey as an email service provider to send out non-survey content).
evidence.answer: Apps not related to facilitating surveys are not permitted to use the API.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Apps which attempt to replicate core functionality of the Services, such as an App which white-labels the Services.
evidence.answer: Apps that replicate core functionality of the Services, such as white-labeling them, are not permitted to use the API.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Apps which facilitate the exporting of API Content for importation into a SurveyMonkey’s competitor’s product or service.
evidence.answer: Apps that facilitate exporting API Content for import into a SurveyMonkey competitor's product are not permitted.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use SurveyMonkey’s Marks as part of the name of your company or of any App or other product or service created by you.
evidence.answer: The developer may not use SurveyMonkey's name or Marks as part of the name of its company or app.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your Apps must be clearly labeled as your own, and not SurveyMonkey’s.
evidence.answer: Apps must be clearly labeled as the developer's own, not SurveyMonkey's.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use SurveyMonkey Marks in a way that creates a sense of affiliation, endorsement, or sponsorship by SurveyMonkey, unless you have SurveyMonkey’s express written permission to do so.
evidence.answer: Use of SurveyMonkey Marks that implies affiliation, endorsement, or sponsorship requires SurveyMonkey's express written permission.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not sell, rent or redistribute access to the API or any API Content to any third party without SurveyMonkey’s prior written approval.
evidence.answer: Selling, renting, or redistributing API access or API Content to third parties requires SurveyMonkey's prior written approval.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey may for any reason demote or remove it from the integration directory.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey may demote or remove the app from the integration directory for any reason.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You will not, and will not allow third parties to, use the API or API Content (or any content, data, output, or other information received or derived from the foregoing) to directly or indirectly create, train, test, fine-tune, or otherwise develop or improve any artificial intelligence systems or machine learning algorithms
evidence.answer: The developer may not use the API or API Content to create, train, or improve AI or machine learning systems, with a narrow exception for inference-time processing.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: General Composio guidance, not SurveyMonkey-specific: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so you do not need your own.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: General guidance: managed apps are the default whenever Composio has one available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: General guidance: to check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a given toolkit, consult the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: General guidance: you provide your own OAuth app or other credentials through a custom auth config for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps: they share quota across all Composio users, while your own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps: managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps: during OAuth, users see a Composio-branded consent message rather than your app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need, so custom scopes may require your own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio."
evidence.answer: Reason to bring your own app: in production, users should see your app name instead of Composio.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Reason to bring your own app: self-hosted or regional variants, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: Composio auth is chosen per toolkit: you can use your own credentials for some toolkits and managed auth for others, each with its own auth config.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: When proxying, the OAuth app's authorized redirect URI is set to your own endpoint, not to Composio's domain.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The example redirect URI for the proxy is an https URL on your own domain at /api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through Composio's backend.composio.dev domain so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: Proxying the redirect through your own domain is optional and is meant for hiding Composio's domain.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately sends a 302 redirect to Composio's callback URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: composio_url = "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback"
evidence.answer: The Composio callback URL that the proxy forwards to is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.
evidence.answer: The proxy must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio; the user's browser must be redirected.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: For toolkits in general (the page does not mention SurveyMonkey), the provider's consent screen by default shows a Composio name, for example on Google and GitHub.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own OAuth app
evidence.answer: For toolkits in general, the documented fix for the Composio-branded consent screen is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: For toolkits in general, bringing your own OAuth app is advised only where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: For some toolkits, the backend.composio.dev URL is also displayed on the consent screen during OAuth.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app.
evidence.answer: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app (no separate developer program or paid plan is named for registration).

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Registering creates a draft app with an access token you can use to query against your account for 90 days.
evidence.answer: Registering creates a draft app with an access token usable for 90 days.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Sm-Apikey: Your Client ID or API key (if you’re using OLD Authentication )
evidence.answer: The webhook section mentions an 'OLD Authentication' option; the page does not say which authentication method is current.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Private apps don’t need to be reviewed by SurveyMonkey.
evidence.answer: Private apps (for your own organization) do not need a SurveyMonkey review.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Every Public app must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey, and must adhere to its terms of use, before it can be published in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account and published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps are the ones available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account once published in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Using the Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys scopes in a Public app requires SurveyMonkey's approval (applies only to these two scopes).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If you’ve deployed a Public app and want to change your scope requirements to include these, you’ll need to contact us at our help center to tell us more about your app and use case.
evidence.answer: For a deployed Public app, adding those approval-requiring scopes later requires contacting SurveyMonkey's help center.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: No other SurveyMonkey accounts can authenticate a draft app.
evidence.answer: Draft apps cannot be authenticated by any SurveyMonkey account other than the owner's; no other accounts can use a draft app.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.
evidence.answer: Private apps can only be used by users in the same SurveyMonkey team who have a paid plan with direct API access.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If you’ve deployed a Public app and want to change your scope requirements to include these, you’ll need to contact us at our help center to tell us more about your app and use case.
evidence.answer: For Public apps, the page says only that the developer must contact SurveyMonkey's help center to tell them about the app and use case when adding approval-requiring scopes; it does not list the review checks.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: The page states that Public apps must adhere to SurveyMonkey's terms of use before publication; no other review criteria are listed.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys are the two scopes that require SurveyMonkey approval in a Public app.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid SurveyMonkey plan to create any collector that is not a weblink collector.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid plan to create any collector other than a weblink collector.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: All Draft and Private apps will initially be subject to request limits of 120 calls/minute and starting at 500 calls/day ( contact sales ).
evidence.answer: Draft and Private apps initially get 120 calls per minute and start at 500 calls per day (the page says to contact sales for limits).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: When a Public app is in draft (during development), it’s subject to draft request limits .
evidence.answer: A Public app in draft (during development) is subject to draft request limits.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Public apps published in our App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day to our API.
evidence.answer: Public apps published in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Before the 90-day draft period ends, you must deploy your app or it’ll be disabled.
evidence.answer: A draft app must be deployed before its 90-day draft period ends, or it will be disabled.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: We permit three violations of up to 150% within a 30-day window. We begin to enforce limits at 100% once your app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.
evidence.answer: Rate limits are enforced at 100% only after the app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days; up to three violations of up to 150% are permitted in a 30-day window.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Our access tokens don’t currently expire but may in the future.
evidence.answer: Access tokens do not currently expire, but may in the future, with developers warned before changes.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey will review all requests within 5 business days.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey says it will review requests for higher rate limits within 5 business days (this is about limit-increase requests, not app review).

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: If you’ve deployed a Public app and want to change your scope requirements to include these, you’ll need to contact us at our help center to tell us more about your app and use case.
evidence.answer: Changing scope requirements on a deployed Public app to include approval-requiring scopes requires contacting SurveyMonkey again.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Private apps have API request limits and higher limits are available for purchase .
evidence.answer: Private apps have API request limits, and higher limits can be purchased.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.
evidence.answer: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.
evidence.answer: Users of a Private app need a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: *Basic plan accounts can access response details for up to 25 responses per survey. Paid plans have unlimited access.
evidence.answer: Basic plan accounts can access response details for only up to 25 responses per survey; paid plans have unlimited access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your Public app uses scopes tied to paid plans, any accounts attempting to authenticate without the necessary plan will be asked to upgrade to proceed.
evidence.answer: If a Public app uses paid-plan scopes, accounts without the needed plan are asked to upgrade before they can proceed.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your app has required scopes , users will need to approve all of them and may need a paid SurveyMonkey plan to successfully OAuth into your app.
evidence.answer: If the app has required scopes, users must approve all of them and may need a paid plan to complete OAuth.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: All required scopes must be approved by and available to the user for the OAuth process to succeed.
evidence.answer: All required scopes must be approved by and available to the user for the OAuth process to succeed.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: During the OAuth process, a user is asked to grant permission to scopes your app is requesting access to.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, each user is asked to grant permission to the scopes the app requests.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri URL encoded OAuth redirect URI you registered for your app (can be found and edited here )
evidence.answer: The redirect URI is the OAuth redirect URI registered for the app, which can be found and edited in the app settings.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The API for the EU datacenter is https://api.eu.surveymonkey.com and the API for the Canadian datacenter is https://api.surveymonkey.ca .
evidence.answer: The API host differs by datacenter: the EU datacenter uses api.eu.surveymonkey.com and the Canadian datacenter uses api.surveymonkey.ca.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Obtain this token in the Settings of your app in the MY APPS tab.
evidence.answer: A Private app's access token is obtained in the Settings of the app in the MY APPS tab.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_id the unique SurveyMonkey client id you got when registering your app
evidence.answer: The client ID is the unique client ID received when registering the app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The client_secret can be found here .
evidence.answer: The client secret can be found at the linked location in the developer settings (the page links it without naming the location).

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You can set scopes to be required, optional, or not required in your app’s settings .
evidence.answer: Scopes can be set to required, optional, or not required in the app's settings.

evidence.question: G11

evidence.answer: Private apps are subject to SurveyMonkey's terms of use.

evidence.answer: Public apps must adhere to SurveyMonkey's terms of use and be approved before publication in the App Directory; no user or install threshold is stated.
